While SCAR has only recommended the above guidelines, it is the conviction of this committee and others with whom this committee has consulted, that an Environmental Impact Statement is both necessary and useful as a means of achieving better integration of individual and group scientific interests. Prior anticipation of possible environmental impacts has enabled the planning of both preventive and curative measures which will accompany the scientific, logistic, and domestic activities of RISP.
This committee, referring to the Guidelines of the Council on Environmental Quality for Preparation of Environmental Impact statements, dated August 1, 1973, and NSF Circular No. 99 (Rev. No. 2) - Environmental Impact Statements, dated February 24, 1974, has concluded that an Environmental Impact Appraisal should be prepared for RISP.
This committee further recommends that a <u>concluding report be filed</u>

<u>at the termination of RISP</u> in which the data on monitoring and a summary

of the salient facts bearing upon the accuracy of the original Environmental

Impact Statement are included.
